title: [Bug]: torch profiler with_stack export kills all vLLM workers with glibc heap corruption (corrupted size vs. prev_size) - 8-node PD-disaggregated DCP16 cluster dies
body:
### Your current environment

<details><summary>Environment (intranet-isolated cluster, manual list instead of collect_env.py output)</summary>

- **Image**: `hcr.meta-guian02.guian.hw-a3.local/antsys/vllm:nightly-releases-v0.27.1rc-a3-openeuler-20260914103752_aarch64` (a3/openEuler nightly image)
- vllm: 0.27.1+empty (source checkout at `/vllm-workspace/vllm`)
- vllm-ascend: 0.19.1rc2.dev1908+g67dd25526 (source checkout at `/vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend`)
- torch: 2.10.0+cpu
- torch_npu: 2.10.0.post4
- CANN: 9.1.0
- triton-ascend: 3.2.2, transformers: 5.14.1
- mooncake-transfer-engine-npu: 0.3.11
- Hardware: 8 × Atlas 800I A3 (910_93) nodes inside a single Atlas SuperPoD (16 NPU dies per node visible to the container)
- Model: Kimi-K3 W4A8 (Ascend quantization, `quantization=ascend`) + DSpark draft (`num_speculative_tokens=7`), `max_model_len=1048576`

</details>

Deployment: PD-disaggregated serving on 8 nodes (4 prefill + 4 decode instances). Each side runs `data_parallel_size=4, tensor_parallel_size=16, decode_context_parallel_size=16` (`dcp_comm_backend=ag_rs`), `multiproc_executor`, chunked prefill, `disable_custom_all_reduce=True`; KV transfer via mooncake (P side MultiConnector wrapping MooncakeConnectorV1).

### Service launch commands

Prefill node rank 0 (other prefill nodes: identical except `--data-parallel-rank`/`--node-rank` = 1..3, per-node `VLLM_HOST_IP`/`VLLM_LOOPBACK_IP`, and `kv_port` = 50012+rank×100). Internal IPs masked as `<prefill-head-ip>`. Note `kv_port` and `kv_role` differ between P and D.

```bash
export VLLM_HOST_IP=<prefill-node-ip> VLLM_LOOPBACK_IP=<prefill-node-ip>
export VLLM_TORCH_PROFILER_WITH_STACK=1   # set to 0 / unset for the no-stack control run (which does NOT crash)

vllm serve /home/admin/model-csi/model \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --tokenizer-mode kimi_k3 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-rank 0 --nnodes 4 --node-rank 0 \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 29500 --master-addr <prefill-head-ip> --data-parallel-address <prefill-head-ip> \
  --api-server-count 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 --decode-context-parallel-size 16 \
  --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 384 --block-size 384 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 --served-model-name kimi-k3 --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 16 --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --quantization ascend --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --skip-mm-profiling --enforce-eager \
  --safetensors_load_strategy prefetch --mm-processor-cache-gb 1 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"vision_chunk":40}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":false,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"enable_fused_mc2":false,"enable_prefill_mc2":false}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_buffer_device":"npu","kv_port":"50012","kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill":{"dp_size":4,"tp_size":16},"decode":{"dp_size":4,"tp_size":16}}}]}}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/home/admin/draft-model","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_tensor_parallel_size":16,"max_model_len":4096,"draft_sample_method":"greedy","enforce_eager":true}' \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"<shared-nfs>/vllm_profile_iter2_withstack","torch_profiler_with_stack":true}'
```

Decode node rank 0 (other decode nodes: identical except `--data-parallel-rank`/`--node-rank` = 1..3, `kv_port` = 60000+rank×100, and non-rank-0 nodes on both sides run `--headless` instead of `--api-server-count 1`; `--master-addr`/`--data-parallel-address` point at the decode head `<decode-head-ip>`):

```bash
vllm serve /home/admin/model-csi/model \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --tokenizer-mode kimi_k3 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-rank 0 --nnodes 4 --node-rank 0 \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 29500 --master-addr <decode-head-ip> --data-parallel-address <decode-head-ip> \
  --api-server-count 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 --decode-context-parallel-size 16 \
  --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 384 --block-size 384 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 --served-model-name kimi-k3 --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter --dtype bfloat16 --async-scheduling \
  --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --quantization ascend --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --skip-mm-profiling \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[16,32,48,64,80,96,112,128],"cudagraph_num_of_warmups":1}' \
  --safetensors_load_strategy lazy --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"vision_chunk":0}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":false,"enable_shared_expert_dp":false,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"enable_fused_mc2":false,"enable_prefill_mc2":false,"enable_reduce_sample":false,"finegrained_tp_config":{"lmhead_tensor_parallel_size":0},"recompute_scheduler_enable":false}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_buffer_device":"npu","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_port":"60000","kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill":{"dp_size":4,"tp_size":16},"decode":{"dp_size":4,"tp_size":16}}}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/home/admin/draft-model","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_tensor_parallel_size":16,"max_model_len":4096,"draft_sample_method":"greedy","enforce_eager":true}' \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"<shared-nfs>/vllm_profile_iter2_withstack","torch_profiler_with_stack":true}'
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**TL;DR: with `torch_profiler_with_stack: true`, stopping the profiler (self-stop via `/start_profile` body `{"num_steps": N}`, or `/stop_profile`) segfaults vLLM worker processes on the torch_npu with_stack path (`!!!!!!! Segfault encountered !!!!!!` bursts, torch_npu signal handler). The engines limp for ~100s (workers hanging, shm broadcast starvation), then every VllmWorker across all 8 nodes dies (`exit code: None`), EngineCore fails on every node, teardown ends with glibc `corrupted size vs. prev_size`, and the whole PD-disaggregated service goes down. Reproduced twice with different collection windows (≈11s and ≈3s). With `torch_profiler_with_stack: false` the exact same flow runs fine.**

Repro steps:

1. Start the service described above; drive load (16 concurrent requests, 20k–40k-token prompts, 700 output tokens, ignore-eos).
2. POST `/start_profile` with body `{"num_steps": 4}` to all engine instances (P and D sides). Returns 200.
3. The profiler stops itself after 4 scheduler steps (~3s window) and starts exporting with_stack profiler data (~73GB across 128 rank directories on shared NFS).
4. ~2 minutes after `start_profile`, worker processes start dying on all 8 nodes within ~35 seconds; each node follows the same sequence: worker death → multiproc_executor shutdown → EngineCore fatal error → `EngineDeadError` → APIServer exit.

Detailed timeline of the second reproduction (log timestamps, first node to die = decode DP1):

```text
06:22:04  POST /start_profile {"num_steps": 4} -> 200 on all instances.
          Profiler self-stops after 4 scheduler steps (~3s), with_stack export begins (~73GB / 128 ranks).
06:22:14  (our redundant POST /stop_profile on all nodes; the API-server-level profiler object answers
          "RuntimeError: Can't disable Kineto profiler when it's not running" — it had already self-stopped)
06:22:14+ immediately after, torch_npu prints bursts of segfault catch messages, e.g. ~17 on the first
          decode node (similar on the other nodes):
              !!!!!!! Segfault encountered !!!!!!!
06:22:24  engine still limping: "Engine 001: ... Running: 2 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 4.4%"
06:23:17  EngineCore_DP1: "No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically
          happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work"
06:23:58  EngineCore_DP1: "Worker proc VllmWorker-7 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor."
          → followed by "[ERROR] TBE Subprocess[task_distribute] raise error[], main process disappeared!" (xN)
06:24:02  EngineCore_DP1 fatal error (traceback below).
06:24:15 - 06:24:34  identical worker-death sequence on the remaining 7 nodes
          (one prefill head node additionally trips, after its workers died:
              File "/vllm-workspace/vllm/vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 366, in collective_rpc
                  assert self.rpc_broadcast_mq is not None, (
              AssertionError: collective_rpc should not be called on follower node
           — likely secondary).
06:24:04+ per-node teardown ends with torch_npu profiler warnings and the glibc abort:
              [W915 06:24:04.180512268 profiler_python.cpp:1185] Warning: `PythonTracer::stop()` was not called. (function ~PythonTracer)
              [W915 06:24:04.180924811 record_function.cpp:255] Requested callback is not found
              [W915 06:24:04.180945241 observer.cpp:122] Warning: Leaked callback handle: 1 (function operator())
              resource_tracker: There appear to be 496 leaked semaphore objects to clean up at shutdown
              resource_tracker: There appear to be 18 leaked shared_memory objects to clean up at shutdown
              corrupted size vs. prev_size
```

EngineCore fatal traceback (decode DP1, first node to die; the other 7 nodes are the same shape):

```text
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1584]   File ".../vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 401, in get_response
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1584]     status, result = mq.dequeue(timeout=dequeue_timeout)
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1584]   File ".../vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py", line 798, in acquire_read
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1584]     raise RuntimeError("cancelled")
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1584] RuntimeError: cancelled
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1351] Traceback (most recent call last):
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1351]   File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1342, in run_engine_core
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1351]     engine_core.run_busy_loop()
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1351]   File ".../vllm/v1/fault_tolerance/engine_core_sentinel.py", line 179, in run_with_fault_tolerance
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1351]   File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 2108, in run_busy_loop
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1351]     self._process_input_queue()
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1351]   File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1536, in _handle_client_request
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1351]     raise RuntimeError("Executor failed.")
(EngineCore_DP1) ERROR [core.py:1351] RuntimeError: Executor failed.
```

Facts that narrow it down:

- **Only with_stack crashes.** Same deployment, same load, same endpoints with `torch_profiler_with_stack: false`: a 3-minute full-load collection (~43GB over 128 ranks) completed cleanly and the service stayed healthy. Normal serving without the profiler runs for hours with no crash.
- **Window size doesn't matter in this range.** Run A used `{"num_steps": 15}` (~11s window, ~69GB) and run B used `{"num_steps": 4}` (~3s window, ~73GB); both crashed with identical signatures ~2–3 minutes after `start_profile`.
- The crash chain is: torch_npu segfault catch bursts right at profiler stop → workers hang (shm broadcast starvation) → workers die by signal (`exit code: None`) → glibc `corrupted size vs. prev_size` at teardown, plus torch_npu `PythonTracer::stop() was not called` (profiler_python.cpp) — the Python tracer is only active in with_stack mode. This points at memory corruption in the with_stack stop/export path of the profiler integration, not OOM (no OOM messages observed; HBM usage far below capacity; export writes to NFS).
- Most of the raw profiler data is already written to `torch_profiler_dir` when the aborts hit, i.e. the crash happens during/after stop, not mid-collection.

Happy to run further diagnostics or test candidate patches on this environment — the failure reproduces reliably on our setup.

body:

```text

Deployment mode: disaggregated prefill/decode
Prefill: 1 instance, TP=8, DP=2, node 192.168.32.41

vllm-ascend: a327c1a6702b39ee2f3ab65eafeae25f0f553640
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When enabling `enable_dsa_cp=true` on the prefill side of a disaggregated GLM-5.3-Flash deployment, the prefill engine fails during startup before `/health` becomes ready.

The same deployment starts successfully when `enable_dsa_cp=false`. With `enable_dsa_cp=false`, GSM8K 256k input performance was verified successfully with TPOT avg `17.1 ms` and TPOT P90 `19.7 ms` at concurrency 8. After switching only the prefill-side `enable_dsa_cp` to `true`, the prefill process fails during cudagraph capture / warmup.

#### Reproduction configuration

Prefill side relevant arguments:

```bash
vllm serve /data3/models/GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 9081 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-rank 0 \
  --data-parallel-address 192.168.32.41 \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 16500 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --quantization ascend \
  --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash \
  --max-model-len 275000 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-config '{"enforce_eager": true, "method": "deepseek_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_npugraph_ex": true, "enable_static_kernel": false}, "enable_cpu_binding": true, "enable_dsa_cp": true, "enable_mc2_hierarchy_comm": false, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true, "recompute_scheduler_enable": true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 96, 128], "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --kv-events-config '{"enable_kv_cache_events": true, "endpoint": "tcp://*:5550", "publisher": "zmq", "replay_endpoint": "tcp://*:6660", "topic": "kv-events"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"engine_id":"0","kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV2","kv_connector_extra_config":{"decode":{"dp_size":8,"tp_size":2},"kv_port":"30000","prefill":{"dp_size":2,"tp_size":8},"use_ascend_direct":true},"kv_port":"30000","kv_role":"kv_producer"},{"kv_connector":"AscendStoreConnector","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backend":"memcache","lookup_rpc_port":"0"},"kv_role":"kv_producer"}]},"kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_role":"kv_producer"}' \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --scheduling-policy priority \
  --safetensors-load-strategy lazy
```

Decode side kept `enable_dsa_cp=false` and was not restarted for this test.

#### Observed result

Both prefill DP ranks fail during startup. The prefill ports `9081/9082` never become ready.

The failure happens while capturing cudagraphs and building SFA context-parallel metadata:

```text
File "/vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend/vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 6100, in capture_model
  cuda_graph_size = GPUModelRunner.capture_model(self)
File "/vllm-workspace/vllm/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 6968, in capture_model
  self._capture_cudagraphs(
File "/vllm-workspace/vllm/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 7099, in _capture_cudagraphs
  self._warmup_and_capture(
File "/vllm-workspace/vllm/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 7023, in _warmup_and_capture
  self._dummy_run(
File "/vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend/vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 4085, in _dummy_run
  attn_metadata, _ = self._build_attention_metadata(
File "/vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend/vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 3806, in _build_attention_metadata
  _build_attn_group_metadata(
File "/vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend/vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py", line 577, in _build
  cos, sin, slot_mapping, parallel_metadata = self._prepare_parallel_metadata(
File "/vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend/vllm_ascend/attention/context_parallel/sfa_cp.py", line 303, in _prepare_parallel_metadata
  assert cos.shape == sin.shape, f"cos.shape must equal sin.shape, got {cos.shape} and {sin.shape}"
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape'
```

Then the worker and engine fail:

```text
RuntimeError: NPUModelRunner init failed, error is NPUModelRunner failed, error is 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape'
EngineCore failed to start.
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'NPUModelRunner init failed, error is NPUModelRunner failed, error is 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape'', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

#### Expected result

`enable_dsa_cp=true` should either:

1. be supported for this GLM-5.3-Flash prefill configuration and start successfully; or
2. fail early with a clear unsupported-configuration error before cudagraph capture, instead of raising `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shape'` in `sfa_cp.py`.

#### Notes

- The deployment is disaggregated P/D with `MultiConnector` combining `MooncakeConnectorV2` and `AscendStoreConnector`.
- The prefill side uses `TP=8, DP=2`, `max_model_len=275000`, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, and MTP speculative decoding config.
- Reverting only prefill `enable_dsa_cp` back to `false` makes the prefill engine start successfully again.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When running GLM-5.2 W4A8 with the V2 model runner, TP=4, DP=2, expert parallelism, SFA, and MTP speculative decoding, concurrent long-output requests can crash the SFA draft model in `torch_npu.npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache`.

The failure is reproducible with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. The target decode runs a full graph, while SFA draft does not use the fused draft-metadata-update path and rebuilds its attention metadata for every speculative step. When DP ranks have uneven numbers of live requests, the draft model executes the DP-synchronized padded token count, but the rebuilt attention metadata contains only the real query rows.

In the failing iteration, one DP rank had three live requests while the synchronized draft model input had four rows:

```text
kv_no_split.shape = [4, 1, 1, 576]

sin.shape         = [3, 1, 1, 64]
```

The issue is timing-dependent because it requires requests assigned to different DP ranks to finish at different times. In the reproduced run, the server became ready at 10:12:52, AISBench started at 10:14:13, and the crash occurred at 10:14:33.

#### Observed result

The target worker first reports full-graph execution:

```text
INFO [aclgraph_utils.py:149] [worker] - run_fullgraph with num_tokens=16
```

The scheduler dump on the failing DP rank contains three running requests, each with four scheduled target tokens (`total_num_scheduled_tokens=12`), while the target graph is padded to 16 tokens.

The draft stack is:

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 2051, in sample_tokens
    draft_tokens = self.speculator.propose(
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 275, in propose
    return super().propose(
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 369, in propose
    decode_fn(

    super()._multi_step_decode(...)
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 526, in _multi_step_decode
    self._generate_draft(
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 405, in _generate_draft
    super()._generate_draft(
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 638, in _generate_draft
    last_hidden_states, hidden_states = self._run_model(
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 381, in _run_model
    last_hidden_states, hidden_states = super()._run_model(
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py", line 430, in _run_model
    ret_hidden_states = self.model(**model_inputs)
  File "vllm_ascend/ops/mla.py", line 277, in mla_forward
    self.mla_attn.impl.forward(...)
  File "vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py", line 1720, in forward
    kv_outputs = self.exec_kv(
  File "vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py", line 1120, in exec_kv
    torch_npu.npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache(
RuntimeError: npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache: NPU function error: call aclnnKvRmsNormRopeCache failed, error code is 107030
```

The corresponding Ascend PLOG reports:

```text
[kv_rms_norm_rope_cache_base_tiling.cpp:439][OPS_BASE][GetShapeAttrsInfo]
OpName:[KvRmsNormRopeCache] cos or sin shape is invalid.
```

#### Root cause

The draft model and draft attention metadata use two different token counts during uneven DP execution:

- The model executes `batch_desc.num_tokens`, which includes the DP-synchronized padding row (four rows in this example).
- Upstream draft attention metadata is deliberately built from the real query count, effectively `batch_desc.num_reqs or num_reqs` (three rows here).
- The SFA RoPE/KV-cache path applies `npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache` directly to the full model tensor without removing the DP-only row, while `cos`, `sin`, and cache slots come from the three-row attention metadata.

#### Expected behavior

SFA draft execution should handle uneven DP batches without passing inconsistent token dimensions to `npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache`. DP-only model padding must not be processed as a real attention query/cache write, and the returned attention output must retain the model tensor's padded shape expected by the surrounding execution path.

title: [Bug][Engram] HOST_UVA shared table blocks A3 startup during post-warmup NUMA migration
body:
## Problem

Engram HOST_UVA with `dp_shared_memory=true` can block A3 worker startup when Ascend CPU binding is enabled.

The current CPU binding path intentionally runs after model warmup and graph capture. It then calls `migratepages` for the whole worker process, moving pages from all NUMA nodes to the NPU-local NUMA node (`vllm_ascend/cpu_binding.py`, `bind_memory`). By that point, the Engram shared table has already been created and registered with CANN HOST_UVA:

- `SharedMemory` creates the shared backing;
- `aclrtHostRegisterV2(..., ACL_HOST_REG_MAPPED | ACL_HOST_REG_PINNED)` registers the complete range;
- the DP-group leader later loads the table.

The shared table is large (about 206 GiB in this configuration), and one physical backing is mapped by the local DP replicas. Migrating the entire worker address space to one NUMA node is therefore expensive and may be incorrect for a shared backing accessed by ranks on multiple NUMA nodes.

## Reproduction

- A3, CANN 9.1
- vLLM pin `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`
- vLLM-Ascend Engram host-offload implementation from #17134
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash W8A8
- D node: TP2/DP8, 16 NPUs, `dp_shared_memory=true`
- V1 runner, `async_scheduling=true`, DSpark with 5 speculative tokens
- `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`
- `enable_cpu_binding=true`

Observed sequence:

1. Model loading and FULL_DECODE graph capture complete.
2. Several `migratepages <pid> 0,1,2,3 <target_numa>` processes remain active for more than 15 minutes.
3. Engine cores repeatedly report `No available shared memory broadcast block found` or wait for the DP coordinator READY message.
4. All D HTTP ports remain unavailable.
5. Terminating the vLLM worker does not immediately terminate the stuck migration helpers; they eventually exit only after a long delay.

This was observed during a real P/D validation run. The same test also confirmed that the issue is in startup/memory placement; no Engram request-level precision failure was reached.

## Questions for discussion

1. Is whole-process `migratepages` after HOST_UVA registration the intended CPU-binding behavior for Engram workloads?
2. Should CPU thread/IRQ affinity be separated from process-wide page migration, with Engram allocation and HOST_UVA registration performed after the affinity is established?
3. For private Engram tables, would NUMA-aware first-touch or `mbind` placement be preferable to post-allocation migration?
4. For `dp_shared_memory`, should the shared backing use an interleaved NUMA policy across the DP group's NUMA nodes, or should HOST_UVA mappings be excluded from generic process migration?
5. Is there an existing Ascend CPU-binding or CANN-recommended pattern for this allocation order?

A short-term workaround is disabling `enable_cpu_binding`, but that is not a satisfactory production solution because CPU binding is needed for performance. We would appreciate guidance on the intended ownership and the least invasive design before changing either the generic CPU-binding path or Engram's HOST_UVA allocator.

title: [RFC]: Support non-contiguous KV cache for hybrid Attention/Mamba and GQA models on Ascend
body:
### Motivation.

Hybrid models such as Qwen3.5 combine Attention KV tensors with Mamba convolution and recurrent state tensors. These tensors have different logical shapes and payload sizes, while the cache allocator may reserve a common, aligned physical page size for cache groups.

A logical tensor's payload size therefore does not always equal the distance between its physical cache blocks. Assuming dense storage can select the wrong address for the next block. Repacking these views into contiguous tensors can also introduce cache copies in the inference path.

Pure GQA models need the same distinction when K and V share a block-major allocation. A contiguous backing buffer can expose non-contiguous K and V views without changing their logical shapes.

We propose supporting these layouts through explicit tensor strides and storage offsets in vLLM Ascend. The objective is to preserve scheduler and block-table semantics while allowing Attention and Mamba operators to access their logical data within the allocator's physical layout.

An implementation is under review in [PR #14340](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14340). This RFC requests feedback on the layout contract, operator integration, and rollout requirements.

### Proposed Change.

1. **Separate logical cache shapes from physical page strides.**

   Derive block strides from the applicable allocation/page contract rather than assuming that a block occupies exactly the product of its logical dimensions. Keep logical block IDs, per-group block tables, and request scheduling semantics unchanged.

   Where the allocator requires a common physical page size, retain that requirement. Independent logical Attention and Mamba views do not imply that their physical page sizes can be chosen independently.

2. **Construct block-major Attention K/V views without repacking.**

   For an eligible combined K/V allocation, construct views using `as_strided`. For the default BBND Attention layout, each K/V view has logical shape `[num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size]`.

   A simplified example with equal K/V payloads is:

   ```text
   Separate dense K/V storage:
       K: [K0][K1][K2]...
       V: [V0][V1][V2]...

   Combined block-major storage:
       [K0][V0][padding][K1][V1][padding][K2][V2][padding]...
   ```

   If each K or V block contains `L` elements and the physical page contains `P` elements, the K/V lane offsets are `0` and `L`, while both views advance by `P` elements between blocks. In the unpadded case, `P = 2 * L`. The individual K/V views are generally non-contiguous even though the backing allocation is contiguous.

   This example describes the combined Attention path, not every supported allocation. Preserve existing separate-K/V, shared-allocation, and backend-specific paths where they have a different contract. Changing the default Attention layout to BNBD is outside this proposal.

3. **Expose Mamba states through their own shapes and offsets.**

   Construct convolution and SSM state views with their respective logical shapes, dtypes, storage offsets, and physical row strides. Do not treat Attention tokens and Mamba states as one concatenated logical sequence. Shared backing storage and slot ownership remain governed by the cache allocator and cache-group mappings.

4. **Integrate the layout in Model Runner V1 and V2.**

   Handle eligible hybrid and pure-GQA allocations in both runner paths, using the kernel block size associated with each cache group. Ensure the MRv2 allocation/binding integration reaches the actual worker entry point. Validate the resulting views, not only the presence of an environment variable or the ability to start a server.

5. **Use stride-aware operator paths.**

   Pass supported strided K/V views directly to Attention operators without forcing a full-cache `.contiguous()` conversion. Validate this behavior separately for each hardware backend, including A5.

   Replace the duplicated AscendC causal-convolution and recurrent GDN implementations with the FLA interfaces `causal_conv1d_fn`, `causal_conv1d_update`, and `recurrent_gated_delta_rule`. Specify a reproducible FLA package/runtime version and ensure the required OPP and operator registration are available in installation and CI environments.

   FLA owns its single-operator numerical tests. vLLM Ascend retains tests for integration behavior such as metadata dispatch and layerwise state updates.

6. **Add indexed Triton helpers for strided SSM state access.**

   Use `gather_ssm_states` and `scatter_ssm_states_` around the GDN path that requires dense selected rows. Gather only requested rows, zero rows when `has_initial_state=False`, and scatter updates back into the original cache. Preserve unselected rows and physical padding.

   The supported layout has contiguous inner dimensions; only the physical state-row stride may contain padding. Indices refer to physical rows and may be unsorted or stored in a strided tensor. Callers must provide valid indices and unique scatter destinations. These helpers are not intended to support arbitrary inner-dimension strides.

   Document the helpers under `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs` and maintain their NPU numerical tests under `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/`.

7. **Add temporary layout observability.**

   During cache initialization, emit debug information identifying the layer, shape, stride, storage offset, physical page size, and contiguity as applicable. These observation points help verify that the intended views reach the runner. Remove them after the mechanism is established.

8. **Validate compatibility and performance before broad rollout.**

   Cover hybrid Attention/Mamba and pure GQA models, Model Runner V1/V2, prefill/decode, graph execution, and MTP configurations. Check read/write correctness and model outputs as well as shape/stride metadata.

   Compare memory use, TTFT, TPOT, and throughput under the same model, hardware, software versions, request lengths, concurrency, and graph/MTP settings. Measure the FLA replacement and Triton state-access changes separately where possible, so their effects are distinguishable from the allocation-layout change. No universal speedup is assumed.

   PD disaggregation and KV connectors need separate checks for memory registration, block sizing, copy boundaries, and transfer destinations. Sparse, compressed, and offloaded cache paths also retain their own contracts. Enabling a local strided view alone does not establish transfer compatibility.

### Feedback Period.

Proposed: at least one week after this RFC is published.

Feedback is requested on:

- Whether the proposed logical-view/physical-page contract is sufficient for both hybrid models and pure GQA.
- Whether the runner integration should remain backend-specific or share more of the upstream allocation interface.
- The FLA version, packaging, hardware coverage, and CI requirements needed for replacing the local AscendC operators.
- The validation required for A5 and connector-specific paths before claiming support for those configurations.

### CC List.

Feedback is welcome from KV cache, Model Runner, GDN/FLA, A5, and KV connector maintainers.

### Any Other Things.

Implementation: [PR #14340](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14340). No additional user-facing CLI option is proposed.

Current validation evidence and remaining work:

- The relocated Triton state-index test passed all 18 cases on an Ascend NPU. It covers dense/padded rows, INT32/INT64 indices, tile boundaries, a real GDN state shape, dtype conversion, and preservation of unselected storage.
- A Qwen3.5-35B-A3B W8A8 smoke test completed MRv2 `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graph capture and single/four-concurrent requests on an earlier revision of the same implementation. This is not a full accuracy or performance acceptance result for the current PR head.
- An MTP=3 configuration also completed startup and graph capture; request validation for that run is still pending. Its draft configuration used `enforce_eager=true`, so it does not establish graph replay for every draft operation. The runtime reported disabled cross-request prefix-cache reuse because the draft KV group could not be identified; this requires follow-up.
- The A5 direct strided-K/V call change is implemented, but A5 end-to-end correctness and performance validation remain pending.
- Full accuracy, controlled performance comparisons, connector compatibility, and CI execution with the declared FLA dependency remain rollout gates.

The RFC does not claim that every integration and hardware combination has already passed validation.

title: vLLM Ascend Roadmap Q3 2026
body:
## Goal

- **ModelRunner V2 adaptation**: vLLM will complete Model Runner V2 migration and ensure new day-0 models are MRV2 only, deprecate MRV1 in Q3. We need to follow vLLM to complete the migration of all features and models on ModelRunner V2.
- **External interface rectification**:
    - The `additional_config` of vllm-ascend has no validation in the code at present. We will complete these validations in Q3, which may expose some previously existing silent errors in `additional_config`.
    - As we previously stated, a large number of environment variables will sunset and be replaced by `additional_config`. Please pay attention to our [external interface documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/user_guide/configuration/env_vars.html).
- **Code rectification**: Due to the emergence of new model structures, development of new features, project progress, and upstream dependency version matching, the current code is severely corrupted and requires refactoring for each module. We will make code improvements to multiple modules, including attention backends, fused_moe, quantization, kvcache, graph, kv connector, etc.
- **New model adaptation**:
    - support new model by default for 90% case.
    - Ensure that features unrelated to the model structure are directly available on the new model without adaptation.
    - Ensure the scalability of the features related to the model structure, and be able to complete the adaptation of the new model within 7days.
- **Engineering Capability**：
    - main2main follow with vLLM in day2.
    - CI time reduced to within one hour.
    - Enhance the quality of RC version, release RC version every two weeks.
    - Increase the number of maintainers to 20+ to enhance feature maintenance capabilities.

## Feature

- [ ] Support custom op incremental compilation.
- [ ] Support DSpark https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/11163
- [ ] Support KVC8/indexerC4 in A5.
- [ ] Long-Context Feature enhancement https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/14582
- [ ] Support layerwise and Sparse KV cache offloading to support longer sequence length https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48203
- [ ] Support layersplit in GLM5.2.
- [ ] Support PP parallelism and features stacking.
- [ ] npugraph_ex support superkernel to reduce TPOT.
- [ ] PD disaggregation and KV pooling support traffic priority control.
- [ ] Support D2rH KV pooling + KV tiered offloading.
- [ ] Support KV pooling in SSD2D/rSSD2D/D2rH/rH2D/share storage2D cases.

title: [Bug][310P]: Qwen3.5-9B-W8A8 TP=1 crashes in QuantBatchMatmulV3 with CANN 9.1.0-beta.1
body:
### Your current environment

- Hardware: Atlas 300I Duo / Ascend 310P3, single logical NPU
- Host architecture: aarch64
- Image: `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.23.0rc1-310p`
- Image ID: `sha256:c91472dc30b204d344a839e02f758da6b9fdc030e74ffec26d69b364f3d060fd`
- CANN in the image: `9.1.0-beta.1`
- vLLM: `0.23.0`
- torch: `2.10.0+cpu`
- torch_npu: `2.10.0.post2`
- Driver: `25.2.3`
- npu-smi: `25.5.1`
- Model: `Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-9B-W8A8-310P`
- Exact model revision: `1bdfd32119177461d7b8f03f01ce100572043c59`
- Quantization: ModelSlim `W8A8_DYNAMIC`
- Tensor parallel size: 1
- Model runner: V1

The checkpoint was fully verified against the exact ModelScope revision, including all LFS object hashes. The model configuration, tokenizer, tokenizer configuration, chat template, vocabulary, and merges are byte-identical to the FP16 checkpoint.

### Reproduction command

```bash
vllm serve /model \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 18111 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5-9b-w8a8 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
  --dtype float16 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --enforce-eager \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --language-model-only
```

### Describe the bug

The checkpoint is recognized as ModelSlim `W8A8_DYNAMIC` and all weights finish loading. Startup then fails consistently during:

```text
EngineCore.determine_available_memory -> profile_run
```

The device DFX log identifies the actual faulting kernel:

```text
QuantBatchMatmulV3_NZ_NZ_int8_int8_fp16_high_performance_21
kernel hash: 5247287448945562503
runtime error: 507015
error: L0C read/write conflict
```

The same failure was reproduced three times:

1. Default multimodal model startup.
2. With `--language-model-only`.
3. With `--language-model-only --max-num-batched-tokens 512`.

The Python traceback sometimes reports a later asynchronous synchronization point such as `aclnnDynamicQuantV2` or `aclnnRmsNorm`, but the device log identifies the same QuantBatchMatmulV3 kernel and hash on every attempt.

### Relevant comparison

On the same 310P server and runtime family:

- Qwen3.8-27B-W8A8 text-only TP=1 has previously started and served a request.
- Qwen3.8-27B-W8A8 TP=2 hit a QuantBatchMatmulV3 failure.
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-W8A8 TP=2 has served requests.
- Qwen3.5-9B FP16 TP=1 runs successfully.

This suggests a shape/tiling-specific W8A8 kernel failure rather than damaged model files, insufficient memory, or general lack of W8A8 support.

### Possible relation to existing issues

This is the same kernel name and hash reported in #10122. A maintainer wrote there that the affected quantization operator has a CANN-side fix in the `9.1.0.beta2` branch. However, the current `v0.23.0rc1-310p` image still contains `9.1.0-beta.1`.

The 310P Model Runner V2 RFC #15577 also says Qwen3.5 W8A8 dynamic support is merged into `main` and remains opt-in with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. The locally available generic `v0.23.0` image cannot be used for this verification because its installed package targets A2 and rejects 310P before model loading.

### Expected behavior / questions

The published 310P W8A8 checkpoint should pass the startup profile and expose a serving endpoint on a supported 310P image.

Could maintainers please clarify:

1. Which current 310P image/tag contains both CANN 9.1.0.beta2 (or the operator fix) and the merged MRv2 Qwen3.5 W8A8 dynamic path?
2. Is this expected to be fixed by switching to that image with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, or is the V1 path in `v0.23.0rc1-310p` also expected to work?
3. If a beta2-based 310P image already exists, we can immediately retest this exact reproducer and provide the result.

title: [Feature]: Support DCP to eliminate duplicated KV cache across TP ranks on DSV4
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Motivation

When using DeepSeek-V4 with TP, the KV cache is currently replicated across all TP ranks.

For example, with TP=8, each TP rank keeps its own copy of the KV cache. Since the attention KV states are not naturally partitioned by TP in this case, this introduces substantial redundant HBM usage and limits the effective KV cache capacity, especially for long-context workloads.

We'd like to use DCP (Decode Context Parallelism) to shard the KV cache across ranks, so each rank only stores part of the cache instead of keeping a full copy.

I'd like to check the current status in vLLM Ascend:

Is anyone already working on DCP support for the DeepSeek-V4 DSA/hybrid KV-cache path?
If work has already started, what parts are currently supported?

Thanks!

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

title: [Feature]: int8 KV cache support for GLM-5.3-Flash / DeepSeek-V4-style hybrid models — decode path fails at aclnnSparseFlashAttention (EZ1009) while prefill path already works
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**The feature we need**: end-to-end support for `--kv-cache-dtype int8` on GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, w8a8, hybrid architecture: MLA + linear-attention/Mamba + compressed-indexer sparse attention (DSA-style), with an MTP head for speculative decoding). Today the config is partially accepted but **the decode path crashes inside `aclnnSparseFlashAttention`**, while the prefill path works on the same build.

#### Why int8 KV is needed (measured, not estimated)

We are trying to serve **512K context** on Atlas A3 (64 GB HBM per NPU, `ASCEND_A3_ENABLE=1`), PD-disaggregated deployment:

- In bf16, per-token KV on this model is ≈24 KB/card — the MLA latent KV is **replicated across TP ranks** (not sharded), plus the indexer cache and mamba page alignment. Measured from `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory`: **one 512K request needs 11.95 GiB KV per card at TP8** (12.16 GiB at TP4), regardless of TP degree.
- Available KV after weights (21.2 GB/card at TP8), HCCL/MC2 communication buffers and the activation profile peak: measured **11.16–11.63 GiB/card** across all configs we tried (gpu_memory_utilization 0.93–0.94, HCCL_BUFFSIZE 400–768, max-num-batched-tokens 128–2048). The engine refuses to start (`ValueError: ... 11.95 GiB KV cache is needed ... estimated maximum model length is 497280`).
- We measured the remaining config levers exhaustively: `gpu_memory_utilization` ≈ +0.2 GiB per 1%, `HCCL_BUFFSIZE` ≈ +0.07 GiB per 100 MB, `max_num_batched_tokens` and `max_num_seqs` ≈ no effect on this check. **bf16 simply cannot fit 512K on 64 GB cards for this model; the hard ceiling we reached is ~497K.**

With int8 MLA KV the requirement halves to ~6 GiB/card and 512K fits with a large margin. This is also consistent with the direction of the existing indexer work ("DeepSeek V4 Ascend **indexer K cache dtype int8**") — int8 MLA latent KV is the natural next step.

#### How we found the problem (in case it helps locating the gap)

1. Our build (vLLM 0.28.0+empty, vllm-ascend-based, with GLM5Next/DeepSeek-V4 patches) already **accepts the config**: `patch_kv_cache_dtype.py` patches `CacheConfig.cache_dtype` to accept `'int8'` ("DeepSeek V4 Ascend MLA KV cache dtype"), and `patch_indexer_kv_dtype.py` accepts int8 indexer K cache.
2. With `--kv-cache-dtype int8`:
   - Memory accounting is correct: the KV memory check passes (requirement halves), page geometry is recomputed (attention block size 1152→2304 tokens at TP4), Mooncake KV registration succeeds, Triton warmup succeeds.
   - **Prefill node (TP8×DP2, enforce-eager): starts up and serves with int8 KV** — i.e. the *prefill* attention path already consumes int8 KV on the very same CANN build.
   - **Decode node: crashes during CUDA graph capture (decode-FULL) on the first decode forward** — see traceback below. `aclnnSparseFlashAttention` reports `EZ1009`: the operator prototype (`OpDef`) has no signature for `key/value = INT8`.
3. Since `EZ1009` is a prototype-level rejection (raised before kernel execution), this looks like an **implementation gap, not a hardware limitation** — int8 KV attention is standard practice and the prefill path already proves the storage/quant layers work on this hardware.

**What we are asking for**:
1. Decode-path support for int8 MLA KV on this model family — either an INT8 K/V signature (with dequant scales) on `aclnnSparseFlashAttention`, or dequantizing the selected KV before the op at the call site (in DSA, decode attends only to the top-k selected tokens, so read-time dequant should be cheap). Clarity on whether the fix belongs in the CANN op registration or in the vllm-ascend call site would help us a lot.
2. KV transfer support for int8 layouts in PD disaggregation (MooncakeConnectorV2 with `use_ascend_direct`), since P and D must agree on dtype/layout.

### Alternatives

- **Keep bf16 KV**: measured ceiling is ~497K on 64 GB cards — cannot meet the 512K requirement.
- **Pipeline parallelism** (PP splits the KV cache by layer, halving per-card KV need): viable in principle, but doubles decode latency and we could not verify Mooncake KV-transfer layout support for PP topologies — a heavy restructuring.
- **max_model_len ≈ 490K**: the business requirement is exactly 512K.
- We would also like to know whether **indexer-only int8** is available as a partial measure, and roughly how much KV memory it saves on this model (we could not determine the indexer cache's share of the ~24 KB/token from the logs).

### Additional context

Crash on the decode node (all TP workers, during `Capturing CUDA graphs (decode, FULL)`):

```text
RuntimeError: call aclnnSparseFlashAttention failed, detail:[PID: ...] Execution_Error(EZ1009):
Failed to execute operator SparseFlashAttention_0. Reason: The dtype or format of the actual input
or output parameter of the operator is inconsistent with that defined in the operator prototype OpDef,
details of parameter are query(DT_BFLOAT16, ND), key(DT_INT8, ND), value(DT_INT8, ND),
sparseIndices(DT_INT32, ND), blockTableOptional(DT_INT32, ND),
actualSeqLengthsQueryOptional(DT_INT32, ND), actualSeqLengthsKvOptional(DT_INT32, ND),
queryRopeOptional(NULL, NULL), keyRopeOptional(NULL, NULL),
attentionOutOut(DT_BFLOAT16, ND), softmaxMaxOut(DT_FLOAT, ND), softmaxSumOut(DT_FLOAT, ND).
```

Environment (from deployment logs; no `collect_env.py` output available — happy to provide on request):

- Model: `/data3/models/GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8`, `--quantization ascend`, `--max-model-len 512000`
- Topology: PD-disaggregated. P: TP8×DP2 (enforce-eager, `kv_producer`). D: TP4×DP4 originally, TP8×DP2 in later tests (`kv_consumer`), `--async-scheduling`, `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`, MTP spec decode (`num_speculative_tokens=3`)
- KV transfer: MultiConnector = MooncakeConnectorV2 (`use_ascend_direct: true`) + AscendStoreConnector (memcache backend)
- Env: `ASCEND_A3_ENABLE=1`, `HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV`, `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FUSED_MC2=1`, `HCCL_BUFFSIZE=400–768`
- SW: vLLM 0.28.0+empty (vllm-ascend-based internal build); CANN version not captured in these logs — will collect if needed.

Related memory observation (separate from this issue, happy to split it out): at TP8, `patch_mamba_config` pads the mamba page size by **14.38%** to align with the 640-token attention block (only 4.86% at TP4). At 512K this padding wastes roughly **1.2–1.5 GiB per card** of KV pool. Fixing this alignment alone would already bring bf16 close to fitting 512K.

I searched existing issues for "int8 kv cache SparseFlashAttention" and found no direct duplicate. Thanks!

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4 DSpark target weights overwrite draft head/HC depending on checkpoint load order
body:
### Your current environment

Reproduced on two ARM64 hosts, each with 8 x Ascend 910B3 (A2), TP=8, DSpark K=7, draft eager, target FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Both EP off and EP on are affected.

Sanitized environment summary collected using `collect_env.py` (deployment-specific addresses and environment variables omitted):

```text
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (aarch64)
Host kernel: Linux 5.10.0-60.18.0.50.oe2203.aarch64
Python: 3.12.13
PyTorch: 2.10.0+cpu
torch_npu: 2.10.0.post4
Transformers: 5.14.1
CANN: 9.1.0
vLLM: 0.28.0, commit 2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a
vLLM Ascend: commit 44f9bf53d93fe6a5b1362b7d81a050d3b0cd997d
Image: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-main
Pinned local ARM64 image ID: sha256:d3e8b2b20036638a285872871696dcded219f6ee751e8070412f57f4189b187d
Model: Eco-Tech/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8
ModelScope revision: 5012d242bcbfb2686702c3fe0c1bfea83cc7d3fb (2026-09-07)
```

The real-model run used `--quantization ascend` and `--model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":128}'`. The minimal loader reproducer below also fails on current Ascend main `0003e1b75`; multithreading is **not** required to reproduce the ordering bug.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.load_weights()` maps the target checkpoint's top-level head/embed/HC keys and the `mtp.*` draft keys to the same destination parameters. When a target key arrives after its MTP counterpart, it silently replaces the trained draft parameter. The result depends on checkpoint iteration/shard completion order.

For example, both `mtp.2.head.weight` and `head.weight` map to `lm_head.weight`. Loading the former and then the latter leaves the draft model using the **target** output head. The same problem affects `embed.weight` and `hc_head_fn`, `hc_head_base`, `hc_head_scale`. The verifier still rejects incorrect proposals, so requests can succeed while speculative decoding loses most of its benefit.

#### Minimal reproducer

Run this in a vLLM Ascend Python environment. It calls the actual loader with tiny CPU tensors and mocked parallel-state accessors; it does not download a checkpoint, initialize a model, or run inference:

```python
from types import MethodType, SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
from vllm_ascend.models.deepseek_v4 import dspark

for draft_first in (True, False):
    head = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(2, 2), requires_grad=False)
    model = SimpleNamespace(
        rotation_path=None,
        config=SimpleNamespace(num_attention_heads=8, num_hidden_layers=43),
        model=SimpleNamespace(num_dspark_layers=3, get_expert_mapping=lambda: []),
        named_parameters=lambda: [("lm_head.weight", head)],
    )
    model._remap_dspark_name = MethodType(
        dspark.DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM._remap_dspark_name, model
    )
    weights = [
        ("mtp.2.head.weight", torch.full((2, 2), 7.0)),
        ("head.weight", torch.ones(2, 2)),
    ]
    if not draft_first:
        weights.reverse()
    with (
        patch.object(dspark, "get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size", return_value=1),
        patch.object(dspark, "get_tensor_model_parallel_rank", return_value=0),
    ):
        dspark.DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.load_weights(model, iter(weights))
    print(f"{draft_first=}: loaded={head[0, 0].item()}, expected=7.0")
```

Observed on unpatched main:

```text
draft_first=True: loaded=1.0, expected=7.0
draft_first=False: loaded=7.0, expected=7.0
```

Expected: `7.0` in both cases. Explicit MTP weights should take precedence independently of iteration order. Global keys should remain fallbacks when the corresponding MTP key is absent.

#### Why the September checkpoint exposes the problem

We compared two local snapshots of the same ModelScope model:

| Checkpoint | Shards | Quantization description | Loader behavior |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Earlier snapshot | 74 | Declares `optional.quarot.rotation_map.global_rotation` | `rotation_path` is set; target head/embed are skipped |
| Revision `5012d242` | 75 | `optional: {}` | `rotation_path=None`; target head/embed may overwrite draft parameters |

Both snapshots contain `optional/quarot.safetensors`, but `get_rotation_path()` uses the metadata rather than file existence. Neither snapshot has `is_rot_used=true`. Full tensor SHA256 comparisons show that the draft LM head, draft embedding and all three draft HC tensors are identical between these snapshots. Within each snapshot, target and draft head/embed/HC tensors differ. Thus overwriting a draft tensor with its target counterpart is not an equivalent substitution.

The quantization scheme also changed, so copying the earlier rotation metadata into the new snapshot is not a justified fix. HC loading is not guarded by `rotation_path` and can still be overwritten on the rotation-enabled path.

#### Regression history

For quantized checkpoints without a rotation path, the direct regression is #13506, merged on 2026-08-07, commit `683b6c009d57714eaf9363f369c7ed4fa0084f5c`. It changed the target head/embed guard from `not self.has_own_*` to `not self.rotation_path` and added target HC loading. Executing the actual loader bodies from this commit and its parent confirms the before/after behavior. The earlier #11431 implementation already had an analogous head/embed ordering issue on the non-quantized path.

#### Real-model evidence and proposed fix

- Before repair, all 8 TP draft-head shards matched the target `head.weight`, rather than `mtp.2.head.weight`; one audited rank also had overwritten HC parameters.
- Holding the running model and test input fixed, repairing draft head/HC restored mean acceptance length from approximately 1.1 to 5.1. This was a diagnostic intervention, followed by a persistent loader fix and fresh model reloads.
- After the persistent fix, all 8 draft-head shards and all draft HC parameters matched the checkpoint. No runtime repair was used for the performance retest.
- C1 pure decode TPOT recovered from **48.70 to 12.20 ms (EP off)** and **49.16 to 12.50 ms (EP on)** on the same checkpoint. These are request-mean TPOT values excluding TTFT/prefill. The private replay request set was held fixed; the repaired result uses two consecutive warm 64-request batches per concurrency/configuration. Across repaired C1/C8 runs, 512 formal requests completed without errors.

Proposed fix: remember which destination head/embed/HC parameters were loaded from `mtp.*`, ignore later target fallbacks for those parameters, and still allow later MTP tensors to overwrite earlier fallbacks. This needs only a small set of parameter names, not checkpoint buffering, and does not change sampling or acceptance rules.

Related symptom report: #13640; its root cause is not established, so this issue does not claim they are identical. #15824 fixes a different Qwen3 DSpark rotation-metadata path and does not address this loader overwrite.

AI assistance: diagnosis, code and regression tests were prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance during the deployment investigation.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

问题说明

一、标题

Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-310p（GDN 混合架构）在 vllm-ascend v0.23.0 上 --enable-prefix-caching 与 MTP 投机解码同时开启时，推理输出 token 级崩坏

二、环境概述

- 硬件：Atlas 300I Duo（310P3，44GB x 4），TP4 使用 NPU 4/5/6/7
- 系统：openEuler 24.03 LTS-SP3 aarch64
- vLLM 0.23.0 + vllm-ascend 0.23.0（CANN 9.1.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4）
- 模型：Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-310p（ModelScope: Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-310p，
  model_type=qwen3_5，64 层 3:1 GDN:full 混合注意力，mtp_num_hidden_layers=1）
- 详细环境信息见 vllm-ascend环境信息/collect_env_output.txt

三、现象

--speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'
与 --enable-prefix-caching 同时开启时，服务加载正常、无任何报错日志、
MTP 接受率指标正常（70%~100%），但推理输出全部 token 级崩坏：

- 短文本："请介绍一下你自己" → 思考段出现"请介绍一下你自己介绍"（复读插入），
  正文输出"我是通义谦"（错字：千问→谦）、"阿里巴巴通义实验室"表述破碎
- 长文本：数字/量词错乱（"500字"写成"50字"、"5000字"）
- 图片/视频用例同样出现错字与破碎复述

关闭 --enable-prefix-caching 后（其余参数完全相同），所有用例输出恢复正常，
MTP 接受率 90% 以上，加速效果正常。

四、复现步骤

（以下命令为可直接执行的 vllm serve 等价命令，模型为本地已下载目录）

【复现（崩坏）】：
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7
vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-310p \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --served-model-name qwen3.8 \
    --max-num-seqs 128 --max-model-len 16384 \
    --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 --dtype float16 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1,4]}' \
    --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_npugraph_ex": false}}'

服务启动后请求：
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"qwen3.8","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"请介绍一下你自己"}],"max_tokens":512}'

【对照（正常）】：上述命令去掉 --enable-prefix-caching 一行，其余完全不变，
重起服务后同一请求输出正常。

五、期望行为

--enable-prefix-caching 与 MTP 投机解码同时开启时，推理输出应与关闭
prefix caching 时一致（或如有已知约束应显式报错/告警），不应静默输出崩坏。

title: [Feature]: Interoperability with vllm-router
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**Feature:** Add support for using the standard `vllm-project/router` (the Rust
router, `pip install vllm-router`) as the front-end for PD-disaggregated
serving on Ascend, i.e. make the vLLM-Ascend Mooncake P2P connector
interoperable with the router's Mooncake PD path (`--vllm-pd-disaggregation
--kv-connector mooncake`).

**Motivation / problem:**

Today, the only supported way to drive multi-instance PD disaggregation on
Ascend is the example script
`examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py`
(adapted from vLLM's NIXL `toy_proxy_server.py`). This works, but it is
explicitly an *example* single-process FastAPI proxy, and it does not scale
well to large deployments. We would like to use the
production-grade `vllm-project/router` instead, as is already possible on the
GPU/Mooncake path.

The blocker is a **handshake-model mismatch** between the router's Mooncake PD
support and the vLLM-Ascend Mooncake P2P connector:

- The router's Mooncake path performs **active discovery**: at startup it queries
  each prefiller's **Mooncake bootstrap server** over HTTP (`/query`) to learn
  the per-DP-rank `engine_id`, then injects
  `transfer_id` / `remote_bootstrap_addr` / `remote_engine_id` into each
  request's `kv_transfer_params`.
- The vLLM-Ascend P2P connector
  (`vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py`) uses a
  completely different, **passive** model: each prefill worker opens a **ZMQ
  ROUTER side-channel** (`handshake_port = side_channel_port + device_index`)
  and exchanges a msgpack-encoded `MooncakeAgentMetadata` on demand
  (`GET_META_MSG` → metadata → `batch_transfer_sync_read`). **There is no HTTP
  bootstrap server and no `/query` endpoint at all.** The `kv_transfer_params`
  (`remote_host` / `remote_port` / `remote_engine_id`) are relayed passively
  through the request/response body by whatever proxy sits in front.

Because the connector exposes no bootstrap server, the router's discovery step
has nothing to query, so the standard router cannot currently be pointed at an
Ascend PD deployment. Users are effectively locked into the example proxy.

**Pitch — a few possible directions (any one would unblock us):**

1. Add an HTTP bootstrap `/query`-compatible endpoint to the Ascend Mooncake P2P
   connector, exposing per-DP-rank `engine_id` in the schema the router expects,
   so the router's existing Mooncake path works unchanged; **or**
2. Provide/document a **passthrough / relay** mode in the router (no bootstrap
   discovery, just relay `kv_transfer_params` from the prefiller response) that
   matches this connector's passive model; **or**
3. Provide an official adapter/shim so the router can drive the ZMQ side-channel
   handshake used here.


### Alternatives

- **Current workaround:** keep using
  `load_balance_proxy_server_example.py`. It functions (flat single pool of
  prefill/decode clients, passive `kv_transfer_params` relay, so multiple
  independent EP groups are transparent to it), but it is a single-process
  example proxy, not intended as a production load balancer, and it lacks the
  routing policies / throughput headroom of `vllm-project/router` at 10s of
  endpoints.
- We considered pointing the router at the connector directly with
  `--kv-connector mooncake`, but it fails because there is no bootstrap server
  for the router to discover (see above).


### Additional context

`vllm-project/router` currently exposes only *active-discovery*
PD modes — either `--vllm-discovery-address <addr>` (external discovery
service) or `--kv-connector mooncake` (which, per the router README/PyPI docs,
"queries each prefill node's Mooncake bootstrap server at startup to learn
engine_id per DP rank"). There is **no passthrough/relay mode** that simply
forwards the `kv_transfer_params` returned in the prefiller's response.

The vLLM-Ascend Mooncake P2P connector provides neither of these: no HTTP
bootstrap server for the Mooncake path to query, and no discovery endpoint for
`--vllm-discovery-address`. It relies purely on ZMQ side-channel metadata
exchange + passive relay of `kv_transfer_params`. As a result the router cannot
currently front an Ascend PD deployment through either mode — this is a missing
capability, not a misconfiguration.

## Environment

- torch_npu: 2.10.0.post6

```
vllm serve /home/admin/model-csi/model --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --served-model-name kimi-k3 \
```

## Case 1 — 9.1.0 base + 9.2.0-built custom ops vendor: `Invalid_Attr(EZ0002)`, activation attribute arrives empty

```
  Invalid_Attr(EZ0002): Attribute activation of MegaMoe has incorrect value .

  Solution: Check whether the operator attribute is correct.
```

vllm-ascend calls `self.mega_moe(...)` (vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py) **without**
passing `activation`, so the CANN python wrapper default `"swiglu"`
(cann_ops_transformer/ops/mega_moe.py: `activation: str = "swiglu"`) applies. The value reaches the
operator as empty — i.e. the attribute is lost between the 9.2.0-built `libcust_opapi.so` and the
9.1.0 framework (op_proto enum is known to the framework, so only the opapi→framework attribute
marshalling is broken). This looks like an ABI mismatch that file-level merging cannot fix.

## Case 2 — CANN 9.2.0 native (no vendor): starts, but garbage output + AICore crash on long prompts

With CANN 9.2.0 (native `cann_ops_transformer.ops.mega_moe` present, `ops/mc2/common` layout), the
same serve command starts cleanly: graph capture succeeds, `MegaMoe symm buffer:
max_recv_token_num is set from mega_moe_max_tokens=65536` logged, 4-node DP4 cluster fully up.

- Short prompt (greedy, temperature=0), repeated runs: output is **garbage**, e.g.

  ```
  Q: 1+1等于几？直接回答数字。
  A: !!..阿. uns桌子上だけ排便 well should但是有一是CRE熄火!!!image不能有肚子疼的控制.!鸽子!...
  ```

- 40k-token prefill prompt: **AICore execution abnormal (EE9999)**, worker dies, engine crash:

  ```
  RuntimeError: query:../torch_npu/csrc/core/npu/NPUEvent.cpp:95 NPU function error:
    acl::AclQueryEventRecordedStatus(event_, &currStatus) ...
  [Error]: The aicore execution is abnormal.
  EE9999: Internal error! rtStreamSynchronizeWithTimeout execution failed
  ```

  Full 4-node service logs: archived (vllm_p_node{0-3}.log, gzipped tar available on request).

## Control — MegaMoe OFF is fully functional on the same setup

Same cluster / model / code, only `--additional-config` without the MegaMoe triple
(`enable_fused_mc2`, `enable_prefill_mc2`, `mega_moe_max_tokens`):

- 4P0D prefill benchmark (cc=12, 120 prompts, 20k-40k text-only, output-len=1): 120/120 success,
  3,343,747 input tokens in 433.84 s ≈ 7,707 tok/s input throughput
- Deterministic math/word-problem accuracy set (200 problems, greedy): **90.0%**, 0 request errors

So the cluster, weight assets, and the standard MoE path are healthy; the failures above are
specific to the MegaMoe path with W4A8 on A3. (The code comment in
`_get_cann_mega_moe_quant_settings` already mentions the W4A8 accuracy root cause being on the
operator side — the garbage output here is consistent with that; the long-prompt AICore crash and
the 9.1.0 opapi attribute loss are additional.)

## Also observed (asset side, for completeness)

Some mounts of the model deliver `quant_model_description.json` with `"optional": {}` while
`optional/quarot.safetensors` and `mm_projector.rot_proj.weight` exist in the index. With that
inconsistent description, `get_rotation_path()` returns None, the projector skips building
`rot_proj`, and weight loading crashes with
`ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'mm_projector.rot_proj'`. Restoring the
`optional` block in the description fixes loading. Worth a check on the model-asset side.

## Ask

1. Case 1: is a 9.1.0-compatible build of the custom ops package (or a version upgrade path that
   also updates the opapi marshalling) available? File merging alone is not sufficient.
2. Case 2: W4A8 MegaMoe on A3 currently produces unusable output and crashes on long prompts —
   is W4A8+MegaMoe on A3 expected to work at this CANN version, and is there a known-good
   combination?

title: [Bug] MRV2 LM-head TP and EPLB collective order hangs idle DP ranks
body:
### Description

The QWEN3_235B_PD nightly job hangs on its first AISBench warmup request when Model Runner V2, LM-head tensor parallelism, and EPLB run together across external DP ranks. The decode API returns HTTP 500 after an HCCL timeout, the proxy returns 502, and AISBench reports `warmup failed`.

Failing run: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35253856165/job/105314153314

### Reproduction conditions

Use vLLM Ascend commit `c7ca0b676b9668535f467b78cff1274a4ddb63b2` with vLLM 0.28.0 and the [QWEN3_235B_PD.yaml configuration at that exact commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/c7ca0b676b9668535f467b78cff1274a4ddb63b2/tests/e2e/nightly/multi_node/external_dp/config/QWEN3_235B_PD.yaml). The YAML on current `main` has since changed, so the pinned revision matters.

- Hardware/topology: three 16-NPU Ascend A3 nodes; one prefill node (TP=16, DP=1) and two decode nodes (TP=1, external DP=32, 16 local DP ranks on each node, EP enabled).
- Model: `vllm-ascend/Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8` with `--quantization ascend`.
- Decode environment: `VLLM_USE_V1=1`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=204`, `HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024`.
- Decode flags: `--async-scheduling --enable-expert-parallel --enable-eplb --max-model-len 36864 --max-num-batched-tokens 256 --max-num-seqs 28`.
- Decode EPLB: `--eplb-config '{"window_size":4000,"step_interval":200,"num_redundant_experts":0,"use_async":true,"log_balancedness":true,"log_balancedness_interval":1}'`.
- Ascend options: `--additional-config '{"finegrained_tp_config":{"lmhead_tensor_parallel_size":8},"eplb_config":{"load_collection_phase":"all"},"enable_mlapo":true}'`.
- Decode graph: `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18]}'`.
- PD transport: `MooncakeConnectorV1`, prefill `kv_producer` (DP=1, TP=16), decode `kv_consumer` (DP=32, TP=1), `use_ascend_direct=true`; the pinned YAML contains the complete connector settings.
- Trigger: run the YAML's AISBench GSM8K chat accuracy case (`batch_size=64`, `temperature=0.6`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_out_len=32768`). It fails during the first warmup request, while one decode DP rank handles work and other ranks run dummy steps. This is the observed reproducer; the individual flags have not been minimized experimentally.

### Observed behavior and diagnosis

The decode logs show DP0 entering an eight-rank LM-head `AllGather` at 17:55:37, while idle DP ranks entered a 32-rank EPLB `AllReduce` starting at 17:55:31. HCCL reports a 204-second collective timeout at 17:59:03. The first warmup request then fails with proxy `Bad Gateway`.

On the active rank, `sample()` calls `compute_logits()` (LM-head collective) before its EPLB step. On idle ranks, the V2 `_dummy_run()` override calls the parent first; the parent advances EPLB before the override calls `compute_logits()`. The two rank paths therefore enter their LM-head and EPLB collectives in opposite order. This ordering explains the timeout and is consistent with the per-rank HCCL traces.

### Expected behavior

Idle and active decode ranks should join LM-head TP before advancing the EPLB step, so the warmup request completes without an HCCL timeout.

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash hybrid (KDA/MLA): single requests with prompt > ~69K tokens hang forever — the four-token-granularity KV cache group receives only ~1/20th of the attention group's capacity
body:
## Follow-up: root-cause refinement + clean calibration data

After further measurement and source reading, we refined the analysis in the original report. The earlier statement that "the four-token group receives only ~1/20th of capacity" was **not accurate** — the actual mechanism is subtler. Corrected findings below.

### Corrected mechanism

The GLM-5.3-Flash hybrid cache has 5 groups (`group_block_sizes=(640, 4, 640, 640, 640)`) sharing **one block-ID space** (`num_blocks`, DeepseekV4-style allocator: `num_blocks = available_memory // Σ(page_size × slots)` in `_get_kv_cache_config_deepseek_v4`, `kv_cache_utils.py:1221`).

Per-request block demand per group:

1. **Four full-attention groups (block_size=640)**: `4 × ceil(tokens/640)` — grows linearly with prompt length.
2. **Mamba group (block_size=4, `mamba_cache_mode="align"`)**: **constant 4 blocks per request** (`1 + num_speculative_blocks`, see `MambaManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1054`) — independent of length.
3. **Indexer K-pool group (`AscendIndexerKPoolStateSpec`, a SWA-MLA group with block_size=64)**: sliding-window demand that **saturates at ≈1,795 blocks for prompts ≳115K tokens** (measured), i.e. a fixed floor.

Because one block ID serves all groups simultaneously, the effective budget for the four 640-token groups is:

```
num_blocks − indexer_saturation(≈1795) − mamba(4) ≈ num_blocks − 1799
```

With `num_blocks=2175` only **~376 blocks** remain for the four 640-token groups → **≈60K tokens per request** → matches the measured admission boundary (68,873 tokens OK / ~72,700 hangs).

### Clean calibration (no prefix hits, usage zeroed after each request, dense 0.3 s sampling)

`num_blocks = 2175`:

| Prompt tokens | Peak `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` | Blocks in use | Decomposition (4×attn + indexer floor + mamba) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11,360 | 31.0% | 674 | 72 + ~598 + 4 |
| 22,745 | 90.3% | 1,963 | 144 + ~1,815 + 4 |
| 37,842 | 91.6% | 1,993 | 240 + ~1,749 + 4 |
| 45,929 | 92.3% | 2,008 | 288 + ~1,716 + 4 |
| 64,645 | 94.4% | 2,053 | 408 + ~1,641 + 4 |

The near-constant block usage beyond ~23K tokens is the indexer group's sliding-window saturation (~1,795 blocks ≈ 115K tokens × 64 tok/block), not a fixed leak.

### Why another deployment with the *same image* does not hit this

An identical-image deployment with `--max-model-len 275000 --max-num-seqs 8` gets `num_blocks = 3612`. Same indexer floor (window is a model property), but the remainder for the four 640-token groups is `3612 − 1799 = 1813` blocks → ≈290K tokens per request. A 207,524-token request (`Delaying free of 51881 blocks`, 4-token kernel blocks) completes successfully there, while `--max-model-len 524400` reduces `num_blocks` to 2175 and fails at ~69K tokens.

### Implication

The admission failure is driven by the **indexer K-pool group's sliding-window floor (~1,795 blocks) being carved out of the single shared block-ID space**. For GLM-5.3-Flash the planner effectively reserves the window regardless of the served request lengths, so `num_blocks` (which shrinks as `max_model_len` grows) becomes the only lever:

- `max_model_len ≤ ~300K` → `num_blocks ≈ 3600` → requests up to ~290K tokens pass.
- `max_model_len = 524400` → `num_blocks = 2175` → requests above ~69K tokens hang.

Possible fixes to consider:
1. Reserve the indexer window lazily (only for requests actually exceeding the window), or
2. Exclude the SWA indexer group from the shared block-ID space (give it its own pool), or
3. At minimum, fail fast with a clear error when `4 × ceil(tokens/640) + indexer_floor + mamba > num_blocks` instead of retrying forever in the waiting queue.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/e8f47fc11c81f3eb3efeb9b40400db8b0fa6eef3/vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L610-L611
# `dispose_layer(kv_b_proj)` breaks live weight synchronization for SFA models

## Summary

`AscendSFAImpl.process_weights_after_loading()` disposes `kv_b_proj` after deriving the SFA kernel weights `W_UK_T` and `W_UV`.

This is safe for inference-only decoding, but it breaks live weight synchronization used by RL systems such as VERL. The `kv_b_proj.weight` parameter remains registered, but its tensor storage is replaced with an empty tensor and its shape becomes `[0]`.

When VERL later sends an updated `kv_b_proj.weight` from the Megatron actor, vLLM resolves the destination parameter successfully but cannot copy the incoming weight into the empty destination. The column-parallel weight loader consequently fails with a shape assertion.

## Impact

This blocks live Megatron-to-vLLM weight synchronization for GLM-5.2/SFA rollout workers.

It is especially problematic with:

```yaml
load_format: dummy
```

## Environment

```text
Model: GLM-5.2
Tensor parallelism: TP=4
Rollout load format: dummy
vLLM: v0.23.0
vLLM Ascend: v0.23.0
Megatron-LM: core_r0.18.0
MindSpeed: core_r0.18.0
Megatron-Bridge: v0.5.0
MindSpeed Bridge: v0.5.0
VERL: v0.9.0
```

## Reproduction steps

1. Start a VERL RL job using a Megatron actor and vLLM Ascend rollout workers, with model GLM5.2 (containing `index_topk` so that `AscendSFABackend` is selected).
2. Configure rollout workers with `load_format="dummy"`.
3. Allow initial model post-processing to run.
4. Synchronize the actor weights to the rollout workers.
5. Observe the failure while loading `model.layers.*.self_attn.kv_b_proj.weight`.

The relevant lifecycle is:

```text
Create dummy kv_b_proj.weight
        │
        ▼
AscendSFAImpl.process_weights_after_loading()
        │
        ├── Derive W_UK_T and W_UV
        └── Dispose kv_b_proj.weight
                shape becomes [0]
        │
        ▼
VERL exports updated Megatron weights
        │
        ▼
vLLM resolves kv_b_proj.weight by name
        │
        ▼
Column-parallel loader tries to copy the incoming tensor
        │
        ▼
Shape assertion fails
```

## Actual behavior

Before disposal, the TP-local parameter has approximately this shape:

```text
kv_b_proj.weight: [7168, 512]
```

`dispose_layer()` ultimately applies:

```python
x.set_(torch.empty((0,), device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype))
```

Afterward:

```text
kv_b_proj.weight: [0]
```

During synchronization, the loader attempts to write a normal `kv_b_proj` tensor or TP shard into the empty parameter and fails:

```text
AssertionError: param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape
```

Representative shapes:

```text
destination parameter: [0]
incoming TP shard:     [7168, 512]
```

The exact incoming shape can depend on where TP sharding is performed, but the destination is no longer a valid two-dimensional parameter in either case.

## Root cause

`dispose_layer()` assumes that the original linear parameter will never be loaded again.

That assumption is valid for inference-only decoding, but not for rollout workers that support live model updates. The optimization invalidates the storage of a registered parameter without making its weight loader reload-aware.

As a result, the model exposes a parameter through `named_parameters()` and `load_weights()`, while that parameter no longer has valid destination storage.

## Suggested fix

Do not dispose `kv_b_proj` when future weight updates are possible:

```python
if not self.live_weight_reload_enabled:
    dispose_layer(self.kv_b_proj)
```

Live reload should be controlled by an explicit configuration/capability flag.

Checking only:

```python
vllm_config.weight_transfer_config is not None
```

may not be sufficient because VERL can use its own ZMQ/IPC transport and call `model.load_weights()` directly.

Checking only `load_format == "dummy"` is also incomplete because a rollout worker may load a real checkpoint initially and still receive later updates.


## Memory tradeoff

For the representative TP-local BF16 shape `[7168, 512]`, retaining `kv_b_proj.weight` costs approximately:

```text
7168 × 512 × 2 bytes = 7 MiB per local SFA layer
```

Inference-only deployments can still use disposal when live reload is explicitly disabled.
